title: Measure decode concurrency 2/4 (p50/p95) on X299
protocol: hybrid --moe-hybrid-max-fetch 1 --moe-cache-auto --max-running-requests 4 (cache 2774), 220032 nvfp4, DISTINCT ~16k prompts, 128-token greedy decode
analysis: Inter-token p50 rises 39 -> 58 -> 83 ms and p95 53 -> 83 -> 208 ms as concurrency goes 1 -> 2 -> 4: every request slows down.
Aggregate throughput does NOT scale (11.8 -> 10.6 -> 10.2 tok/s): the shared PCIe expert gather is the bottleneck, so more concurrent requests just share it.
This matches the 45 finding on identical-prompt radix sharing; with distinct prompts concurrency is net-negative, which is why prod uses --max-running-requests 1.
decision: informational: keep prod at max-running-requests 1 (single-request speed); concurrency offers no aggregate gain on this box.
limitations: 16k prompts, mr=4 test server (prod is mr=1); hybrid config. p50/p95 from inter-token arrival stamps in the client stream.
